key_insight: Cu feedstock morphology governs impact deformation in cold-sprayed Cu–Al₂O₃ composites: spherical particles localize strain at splat interfaces, while spongy particles distribute strain through collapsing ligaments.
engineering_relevance: Feedstock morphology provides a design lever alongside spray parameters for tailoring composite microstructure and mechanical performance.
method: Compare deposits produced using spherical and spongy Cu feedstocks.
Evaluate mechanical and tribological behavior using micro-compression and wear analyses.
evidence_signal: Multi-scale characterization links spherical Cu to refined splat boundaries and larger core grains, and spongy Cu to distributed strain hardening and enhanced ceramic encapsulation, even at comparable reinforcement fractions.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance gains or processing window, limiting assessment of morphology-selection benefits for specific applications.
paper_title: Feedstock Morphology Governs Impact-Induced Deformation in Cold Sprayed Metal-Ceramic Composites
